conventions.convention: Coefficients are F₂. Multiplication by U lowers both integer filtration coordinates by one and Maslov grading by two. Epsilon is 1 when F_tau vanishes, −1 when G_tau vanishes, and zero when both maps are nonzero.
Upsilon is −2 times the minimum weighted filtration over Maslov-zero cycles representing the normalized total-homology generator; a chain's filtration is the maximum over its supported terms.
The real-series coefficient ring has well-ordered nonnegative real support. The t-modification uses U=v² and reweights the differential; it is not ordinary scalar extension of that differential.
Grid Upsilon uses the ordinary quotient identifying all marking variables. Its maximal non-torsion grading defines the function on [0,1]; values above 1 are defined by reflection t ↦ 2−t.
Stable equivalence uses Maslov-graded bifiltered maps and homotopies. Added summands have zero total homology; associated-graded acyclicity is not required.
The concordance inverse −K is the reverse mirror. The genus bound concerns smooth properly embedded surfaces, not locally flat topological surfaces.

load_bearing.statement: For fixed t ∈ [0,2], the weighted filtered complex admits a filtered graded decomposition C=T⊕A, where T is generated by a normalized representing cycle at filtration nu_t(C), A is totally acyclic, and the maximal non-torsion t-modified grading is −2nu_t(C).

Stable filtered equivalence preserves epsilon. Epsilon changes sign under reverse mirror, epsilon=0 implies tau=0, and the stated equal-sign and zero-factor tensor rules hold. The displayed torus/cable knot has tau=0 and epsilon=1; the trefoil and its double both have epsilon=1.
The least integer s for which delta(A(K,s))=0 exists and satisfies 0 ≤ nu-minus(K) ≤ g₄ˢᵐ(K).

A smooth oriented knot smoothly concordant to the unknot has its normalized knot Floer complex stably Maslov-graded bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to the unknot complex, using finite-rank free totally acyclic summands.

Upsilon is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, vanishes at zero, is symmetric under t ↦ 2−t, has initial right derivative −tau, is additive under connected sum, changes sign under reverse mirror, and satisfies |Upsilon_K(t)| ≤ t g₄ˢᵐ(K) for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1.
For every knot grid G and every t ∈ [0,2], Upsilon_G(t)=Upsilon_K(t), retaining the ordinary-collapse factor with generator bidegrees (0,0) and (−1,−1).

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly declared countable-choice assumption on the analytic knot Floer and concordance supplier branches; distinguished from full AC.
The separately retained full-choice dependencies and their distinction from the analytic countable-choice assumptions.

concerns.concern: Fact F1 attributes to the epsilon definition the characterization 'epsilon is 1 when the distinguished vertical class is a horizontal boundary, −1 when it is not a horizontal cycle'. The cited definition instead uses the exact hook maps F_tau and G_tau. Horizontal representative language requires a suitable representative or simplification convention; it is not a test on an arbitrary representative. The same batch's epsilon lemma explicitly cautions in step 3.1 that a chosen horizontal noncycle alone is not an epsilon test. The worked proof itself correctly computes the hook maps, so this does not invalidate its numerical conclusions.

seams_checked.note: The consumers distinguish restriction to a chosen variable action from ordinary simultaneous collapse. They retain the extra (0,0),(−1,−1) factors and use the normalized filtered comparison and its stated analytic prerequisites. The t-modification supplier permits the column-finite maps needed after restriction of scalars.

The diagramwise tau definition is distinguished from model independence. The connected-sum supplier explicitly supplies the full normalized bifiltered tensor equivalence used here. The tau cobordism inequality is not strengthened into a nu-minus estimate or slice splitting; those have separate, explicit external inputs.

The epsilon witnesses use the positive Clifford-torus slope convention for T(2,5), T(4,5), and the trefoil. Their Floer staircases are supported by separate grid computations rather than attributed to the torus-knot definition.

The geometric admissions use signed visit data, crossing rotations, orientations, and a selected outer face. The trefoil argument explicitly reconciles outer-face choices before invoking reconstruction uniqueness; it does not claim that distinct codes automatically determine the same knot.
